links.comparator_used: No unassisted-clinician arm; ChatGPT-4 output was compared with human expert annotations as the gold standard and expert Likert ratings of rephrasing
links.outcome: Identification of stigmatizing language (precision, recall, F1) and quality of rephrasing (de-stigmatization, faithfulness, conciseness, clarity)
links.effect: Overall identification micro-F1 = 0.51; per-category micro-F1 = 0.69-0.91; rephrasing scored 2.7 for de-stigmatization, 2.8 for faithfulness, and 3.0 for conciseness and clarity (three-point scale)
links.tradeoff: Limited automatic identification accuracy overall; performance was significantly affected by prompt design; authors recommend human oversight
links.quote: ChatGPT showed poor overall identification (micro-F1 = 0.51) but moderate-to-high performance across individual stigmatizing language categories (micro-F1 = 0.69-0.91).

design_hint: prompt design variation for stigmatizing language identification
